base_member_text: [L135-L136,L233-L234] (LOW/output-consistency) Three-panel figures use different aspect ratios for PNG and EPS exports.
audit_member_text: [L135-L136,L233-L234] (LOW/export-consistency) Three-panel PNG exports use a 3:1 size while their EPS counterparts use 2:1, yielding inconsistent aspect ratios and layout across output formats.

base_member_text: [L287-L298] (MED/graphics-portability) Contour reconstruction assumes contour objects expose patch children with scalar FaceVertexCData, making the helper dependent on a particular graphics-object representation.
audit_member_text: [L287-L305] (MED/graphics-api-assumption) Contour extraction assumes contourf exposes patch children with scalar FaceVertexCData, so graphics implementations with different contour objects can leave the polygon arrays empty and make reindexing fail.

adversarial.rationale: The enclosing helper only collects patch children and has no fallback from an empty xp/lp before ismember and reindexing. The [MathWorks R2014b compatibility explanation](https://blogs.mathworks.com/loren/2014/11/05/matlab-r2014b-graphics-part-3-compatibility-considerations-in-the-new-graphics-system/) confirms Contour objects no longer expose those children; the fixed callers supply nonempty contour levels and have no version guard.

base_member_text: [L316-L322] (MED/polygon-topology) Removing NaN separators before creating a patch joins disconnected polygon segments and can fill regions that should remain separate.
audit_member_text: [L316-L322] (MED/polygon-topology) Removing all NaN separators before creating one patch joins separate polygon rings and can fill regions or holes that the original contour kept separate.

adversarial.rationale: This is a latent LOW topology limitation only when a collected patch actually contains multiple rings separated by NaNs; deleting a lone trailing separator does not join rings. The only callers use fixed rectangular meshes and smooth depth/period or height/depth fields, so the cited lines do not establish ring corruption in the generated figures; changed inputs or a different contour representation are needed.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

base_member_text: [L151-L152,L249-L250] (MED/graphics-contract) Combined plots select exactly four patches by child order without validating their count or associated contour levels.
audit_member_text: [L151-L152,L249-L250] (MED/plot-selection-contract) Combined plots copy exactly four patches by child order rather than threshold identity, making the selected boundary regions depend on contour count and graphics stacking order.

base_member_text: [L300-L305] (MED/contour-mapping) Reordering patches by contour level alone collapses distinct same-level contours and uses unchecked zero indices when a level has no match.
audit_member_text: [L300-L305] (MED/contour-identity) Polygons are matched only by contour level, so multiple disconnected polygons at the same level reuse one matching patch and can lose or duplicate geometry.
[L301-L305] (MED/index-validation) The ismember result is used directly as an index without checking for zero, so any contour level absent from the extracted patch data causes invalid indexing.

adversarial.rationale: The level-only ismember lookup really reuses one index when lp contains duplicate levels, but that requires multiple collected patches at the same level. Narrow to a LOW latent limitation for disconnected contour components: the actual callers use the fixed smooth fields at L8-L20, rather than an arbitrary multi-island surface, and no such duplicate-component case is established.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check
